title: U.S. House · Utah's 2nd District
area: Northern Utah under the congressional map first used in 2026, drawn by a Third District Court after the Legislature's 2021 map was struck down; largely overlaps the old 1st District, including Ogden and parts of Davis and Weber counties.

context.text: Utah's congressional map was redrawn for 2026 by court order in League of Women Voters v. Utah State Legislature. As a result, incumbent Blake Moore — who represented the old 1st District — is running for this newly drawn 2nd District rather than a district with the same boundaries he previously held. Moore defeated Karianne Lisonbee 57.8%-42.2% in the June 23, 2026 Republican primary.

candidates.name: Blake Moore
candidates.ballotNote: Defeated Karianne Lisonbee 57.8%-42.2% in the June 23, 2026 Republican primary
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative, Utah's 1st District (since 2021); Vice Chair of the House Republican Conference

summary.text: Blake Moore is the Republican incumbent seeking re-election, running in the newly drawn 2nd District after representing the old 1st District since 2021. A native of Ogden, he worked in the U.S. Foreign Service and as a Principal at the Cicero Group before entering Congress, and since 2023 has been Vice Chair of the House Republican Conference. He sits on the Ways and Means and Budget committees and is running on tax cuts, economic growth and support for Hill Air Force Base.

background.text: Born in Ogden, Utah, in 1980; his House website describes him as a native of Ogden.

According to his House website, he served a mission for the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints in Seoul, South Korea, and signed a scholarship to play quarterback at Utah State University before graduating from the University of Utah; he was also named a Wendy's National High School Heisman winner and is an Eagle Scout. He earned a B.A. in behavioral science and health from the University of Utah and an M.A. in public policy and administration from Northwestern University.

Served in the Foreign Service of the U.S. Department of State and worked abroad in business development in the healthcare and financial services industries, including as an international healthcare consultant with DocBerry International.
Worked as a Principal at the Cicero Group, a Utah-based consulting firm, on social impact, market research and strategy projects before running for Congress.
Elected to the U.S. House in 2020, succeeding Rep. Rob Bishop, and took office January 3, 2021; in his first term he served on the Armed Services, Natural Resources and Budget committees.

According to his House website, four bills he sponsored were signed into law in his first term: the Saline Lake Ecosystems in the Great Basin States Program Act, the Better Cybercrime Metrics Act, the National Medal of Honor Act and the Modernizing Access to our Public Land Act.
Elected Vice Chair of the House Republican Conference in November 2023; his House website says he is the first Utahn elected to House or Senate leadership. He also served as an Assistant Whip.

In the 119th Congress (2025-2026) he serves on the Committee on Ways and Means (Health, Social Security and Trade subcommittees), which his House website describes as a first for a Utah Republican, and on the Committee on Budget.

Convened a Debt and Deficit Task Force in Ogden and was named a 2022 Fiscal Hero by the Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget, according to his House website; he co-chairs the Depot, Air Force and Future caucuses.
His House website says he is married to Jane Boyer and they have four sons.

priorities.text: Says he helped draft tax-cut legislation that doubled the child tax credit, ended taxes on tips, car-loan interest, Social Security benefits and overtime, and increased wages "by up to $7,200 per worker."
As co-chair of the House Air Force Caucus and House Depot Caucus, says he has worked to secure funding and infrastructure for Hill Air Force Base and Utah's defense workforce.
Says he prioritizes secure borders and a "lawful immigration system," and supports House Republican border security legislation.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Ways and Means (Health, Social Security, and Trade subcommittees) and the House Committee on Budget in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

candidates.name: Peter Crosby
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Democratic primary without appearing on the ballot after the primary was canceled; also withdrew from the 1st District Democratic primary earlier in 2026

summary.text: Peter Crosby is the Democratic nominee for Utah's 2nd Congressional District and a first-time candidate from Cache Valley. He earned two degrees from Utah State University and works as a director and project manager for a research company serving higher education. According to his Ballotpedia survey, his campaign messages include ending the tariff regime, revising the corporate tax code and expanding access to health care.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from Utah State University in 2011 and a graduate degree from Utah State University in 2013; describes both degrees as being in political science.

Says he was in the ROTC program at the University of Utah before an accident during physical training ended his military career, and describes himself as an Eagle Scout from a family with a long history of military service.
Career experience includes work as a project manager, a corporate analyst and an adjunct professor; he says he has more than twenty years of combined public- and private-sector experience.
Currently a director and project manager for a research company that supports higher-education institutions, according to his Ballotpedia survey.
Describes himself as a first-time candidate. Won the Democratic nomination at the April 25, 2026 party convention, and the Democratic primary was then canceled.
Says he and his wife, Amanda, have been married for over 20 years, have three daughters and are raising their family in Cache Valley.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website content or detailed public policy statements were found beyond his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey and biographical facts.

candidates.name: Carlton Bowen
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the April 10, 2026 Independent American Party of Utah convention
candidates.currentRole: State Chair, Independent American Party of Utah (self-described)

summary.text: Carlton Bowen is the Independent American Party of Utah nominee for Utah's 2nd Congressional District. An Air Force veteran, he works as a senior IT project manager at Intermountain Healthcare, previously served on the American Fork City Council and was the party's 2024 U.S. Senate nominee. He says he is running to defend constitutional freedoms.

background.text: Born and raised in Utah; graduated from Hillcrest High School.
Served in the U.S. Air Force from 1988 to 1994; earned an associate degree in imagery and intelligence analysis from the Community College of the Air Force.
Earned a bachelor's degree in economics from Weber State University and, according to his survey, graduated cum laude.
Works as a senior IT project manager at Intermountain Healthcare; has also worked as a program manager, instructor, consultant and team lead.
Served on the American Fork, Utah city council; he describes himself as a former council member.

Won the Independent American Party of Utah convention on April 27, 2024 and appeared on the November 2024 ballot for U.S. Senate, which John Curtis won; Bowen says he received 83,972 votes statewide and took part in the Utah Debate Commission's three-way Senate debate.
Describes himself as State Chair of the Independent American Party of Utah.
Says he married his wife, Linda, 38 years ago, and that they raised six children in Utah and have sixteen grandchildren.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website content was found; biography draws on Ballotpedia and his 2026 Candidate Connection survey.

candidates.name: Daniel Cottam
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the April 18, 2026 Libertarian Party convention

summary.text: Daniel Cottam is the Libertarian Party nominee for Utah's 2nd Congressional District. A bariatric surgeon who founded healthcare businesses, he has previously run as a Libertarian for governor in 2020, the Utah House in 2022 and Utah's 1st Congressional District in 2024. In his 2024 Ballotpedia survey he said he was running on balanced budgets and Medicare reform.

background.text: Born in Salt Lake City, Utah; graduated from Cypress Creek High School.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Brigham Young University in 1993 and an M.D. from the University of Texas Health Science Center at San Antonio in 1997.

Career experience includes working as a bariatric surgeon, a business owner and a consultant with Medtronic; in 2024 he said he practiced surgery in the then-1st District and had started four healthcare businesses.
Said in his 2024 survey that he had been registered as both a Republican and a Democrat before registering as a Libertarian at age 50.
Ran as the Libertarian candidate for Utah governor in 2020 (3.5%), for Utah House District 20 in 2022 (5.7%) and for U.S. House in Utah's 1st District in 2024 (4.8%), losing each time.
Said in 2024 that he is married and has five children.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website content or 2026 Candidate Connection survey was found; the survey cited here is from 2024.

summary.text: Robert Moesinger is an unaffiliated candidate for Utah's 2nd Congressional District. A systems and automation engineer who describes himself as not a politician, he is running primarily on replacing the two-party system with multi-party democracy, including ranked choice voting in multi-member House districts.

background.text: Graduated from Ogden High School and earned a graduate degree from the University of Utah in 2018.
Works as a systems and automation engineer, studying manufacturing systems, analyzing data and correcting process flaws, according to his survey.
Describes himself as a first-time, non-politician candidate and a Utah father who plays board games with his family; says his faith is the foundation of his moral framework.

priorities.text: Argues the core problem in American politics is the two-party system itself, which he says creates bad incentives for representatives; supports moving toward a multi-party system to increase voter choice and legislative independence.
priorities.quote: An election that sends a Republican or Democrat to their respective Washington trench fortifies the dominance and dysfunction of the two parties.
